scenario: 法律 AI 要在几百份、合计约 10 万页的文档上回答问题，先得把它们变成一个可检索的知识库。
scenario_en: A legal AI must answer questions over hundreds of files totaling ~100K pages, so you first turn them into a searchable knowledge base.
q: RAG 离线索引管线的正确步骤顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the correct order of the RAG offline indexing pipeline?
why: 离线一次性把文档切成可单独检索的小块、转成向量、连同元数据存进向量库；查询时才检索。顺序错了检索就无从谈起。
why_en: Offline you parse, chunk, embed, and store vectors with metadata once, so that at query time you can retrieve only the relevant pieces.
diagram:
flowchart LR P["解析 Parse"] --> C["切块 Chunk
~200-1000 tok, overlap"] C --> E["Embedding"] E --> V["向量库 + 元数据
file / page / chunk_id"]
options: 先对整份文档整体做一次 embedding，再按向量聚类结果切块，最后把每块连同向量和元数据一起存进向量库
跳过切块，直接把整份原始文档原样存进向量库，等查询命中时再即时切块和 embedding
解析 → 切块(带 overlap) → embedding → 存向量库 + 元数据(文件/页/chunk_id)
先在这几百份文档上微调训练一个法律专用模型，再让它直接回答、不走检索
options_en: Embed the whole document once first, then chunk by vector clusters, then store each chunk with its vector and metadata.
Skip chunking, store whole raw documents as-is in the vector store, and chunk plus embed on the fly at query time.
Parse, chunk (with overlap), embed, then store in a vector DB with metadata (file/page/chunk_id).
Fine-tune a legal-specific model on these documents first, then answer directly with no retrieval.
optionMeanings: 先整体 embedding 再切块：把 embedding 当成切块前的预处理
整份不切原样入库：把向量库当普通文档存储用
标准离线管线：解析→切块→逐块 embedding→带元数据入库
为知识库微调专用模型：走训练而非检索的路线
optionMeanings_en: Embed the whole doc first, treating embedding as a pre-chunking step.
Store whole docs uncut, using the vector store like plain document storage.
The standard offline pipeline: parse, chunk, embed per chunk, store with metadata.
Fine-tune a dedicated model per knowledge base — training instead of retrieval.
optionScenarioImpacts: embedding 只能作用在已切好的 chunk 上，顺序反了整条跑不通
10 万页整份远超上下文、也无法细粒度命中，检索名存实亡
元数据(文件/页/chunk_id)让每条答案可溯源，正是要的结构
每换一批文档就重训，成本高又违背 RAG 即插即用的初衷
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Embeddings run per chunk, so reversing the order breaks the whole pipeline.
100K pages far exceed the context and block fine-grained hits, so retrieval is retrieval in name only.
Metadata (file/page/chunk_id) makes every answer traceable — exactly the structure you want.
Retraining per document batch is costly and defeats RAG's plug-and-play point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索增强生成：查询时先检索外部知识，再让 LLM 基于它作答。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) fetches external knowledge at query time and has the LLM answer grounded in it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把长文档切成的可单独检索的小段文本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A chunk is a small piece of a long document that can be retrieved on its own.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把文本转成向量，语义相近的文本在向量空间里距离近。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding turns text into a vector so semantically similar texts land close together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门存储和按相似度检索向量的数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector DB stores embeddings and searches them by similarity.

optionDirectness: 只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
optionDirectness_en: Only fits when this statement is true: embed the whole document once first.
Only fits when this statement is true: skip chunking.
Use when offline you parse, chunk, embed, and store vectors with metadata once, so that at query time you can retrieve only the relevant pieces.
Only fits when this statement is true: fine-tune a legal-specific model on these documents first, then answer directly with no retrieval.

scenario: 切块时如果按固定字符硬切，一句关键条款可能被拦腰截断，落在两个 chunk 里都不完整。
scenario_en: If you split by fixed character count, a key clause can be cut in half and end up incomplete in two chunks.
q: 该怎么切块才利于检索？
q_en: How should you chunk for good retrieval?
why: 按语义边界切成 ~200-1000 token、相邻块留 overlap，既保证每块语义完整、又不因边界截断而漏掉跨界的句子。块太大稀释相关性、太小丢上下文。
why_en: Chunk on semantic boundaries at roughly 200 to 1000 tokens with overlap so each chunk is self-contained and boundary-spanning sentences are not lost.
tradeoff: 大块(上下文全但相关性稀释) vs 小块(精准但易丢上下文)
options: 每 5000 字符硬切一刀，不留 overlap
按语义边界切成 ~200-1000 token，相邻块留 overlap
整篇文档当作一个 chunk
每个句子单独当一个 chunk，永不重叠
options_en: Hard-split every 5000 characters with no overlap.
Split on semantic boundaries at ~200-1000 tokens with overlap between neighbors.
Treat each whole document as one chunk.
Make every single sentence its own chunk with no overlap.
whenOtherWins: 如果文档本身是结构化短条目(FAQ、字典条目)，一条一 chunk、无需 overlap 反而更干净。
optionExplanations: 硬切会把一句话截成两半，两个 chunk 都不完整，检索时任一块都不够作答。
对；语义边界 + overlap 让每块自洽，跨边界的句子也不会被漏掉。
整篇一个 chunk 检索粒度太粗，命中后还是塞不进上下文、相关性也被稀释。
句子级过碎会丢掉上下文，一个指代或前提可能落在别的句子里。
optionExplanations_en: Hard-splitting cuts sentences in half, leaving both chunks incomplete and neither sufficient to answer.
Correct — semantic boundaries plus overlap keep each chunk self-contained and avoid losing boundary-spanning sentences.
One chunk per document is too coarse to retrieve and still dilutes relevance and overflows the context.
Sentence-level chunks are too fragmented and drop context, since a referent or premise may live in another sentence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 相邻 chunk 之间重叠一小段文本，避免边界句子被切断丢失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Overlap repeats a small span between neighboring chunks so boundary sentences are not lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型处理文本的最小单位，约等于一个词或词的一部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A token is the model's basic text unit, roughly a word or part of a word.

q: 补全 RAG 在线查询的完整步骤。
q_en: Fill in the full RAG online query path.
why: 在线路径是：query 向量化 → top-k 检索 → rerank 精排 → 带引用塞进 prompt → 生成。rerank 提升 precision，citation 让答案可溯源。
why_en: The online path embeds the query, retrieves top-k, reranks, stuffs cited chunks into the prompt, then generates.
text: 在线查询：问题 embedding → {{top-k}} 检索(可加关键词做 hybrid) → {{rerank}} 精排 → 把带 {{citation}} 的相关 chunk 塞进 prompt → 生成答案。
text_en: Online query: embed question, {{top-k}} retrieve (optional keyword hybrid), {{rerank}}, stuff relevant chunks with {{citation}} into the prompt, then generate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索时取相似度最高的前 k 个 chunk。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-k retrieval returns the k most similar chunks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对初步召回的候选用更精的模型重新排序，提升前排相关性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reranking re-orders retrieved candidates with a more precise model to improve top relevance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 答案里标注它来自哪个文件、哪一页，供核查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A citation marks which file and page an answer came from, so it can be verified.

scenario: 法律任务要在 10 万页记录里回答问题，关键事实分散在第 1 万、2 万、4 万、5 万页多处；标准 top-k 只取最相关的少数几个 chunk。
scenario_en: A legal task must answer over 100K pages where key facts are scattered across pages 10k/20k/40k/50k, but standard top-k returns only a few most-relevant chunks.
q: 要保证「一处都不漏」(召回/完整性)，该用什么？
q_en: To guarantee completeness (recall) and miss nothing, what do you use?
why: top-k 优化的是 precision——取最相关的几块，会静默漏掉稀疏散落的事实。要「不漏」必须 touch 每个 chunk：map(并行逐块抽取) → reduce(聚合)，这才覆盖全量拿到 recall。
why_en: Top-k optimizes precision and silently misses thinly scattered facts, so for completeness you must touch every chunk via map-reduce: map extracts per chunk, reduce aggregates.
tradeoff: top-k(precision, 快但会漏) vs map-reduce(recall, 全覆盖但贵)
diagram:
flowchart TB Q1["Top-k 检索"] --> R1["取最相关的几块"] --> A1["precision 高
但可能漏掉散落事实"] Q2["Map-Reduce"] --> M2["map: 并行处理每个 chunk"] --> RD2["reduce: 聚合"] --> A2["touch 全部
拿到 recall/完整性"]
options: 把 top-k 从 5 调到 1000，一次取更多 chunk
把全部 10 万页拼成一个超长 context 让模型一次读完
换一个更强的 embedding 模型提升相关性排序
对每个 chunk 做 map(并行抽取)再 reduce(聚合)，遍历全部 chunk
options_en: Raise top-k from 5 to 1000 to pull in more chunks.
Concatenate all 100K pages into one huge context for a single read.
Swap in a stronger embedding model to improve relevance ranking.
Map every chunk (extract in parallel) then reduce (aggregate), touching all chunks.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是找某一条明确条款(一个具体事实)，top-k 检索又快又够，不必扫全量付 map-reduce 的成本。
optionMeanings: 调大 k：仍按相似度排序，只是多取几百块候选
超长上下文：把 10 万页塞进一个 prompt 硬读
换 embedding 模型：只改召回时的相关性排序
map-reduce：逐块抽取再聚合，强制走遍全量
optionMeanings_en: A bigger k still ranks by similarity, just pulls a few hundred more candidates.
Long context: cram all 100K pages into one prompt and read them at once.
A new embedding model only changes the relevance ranking at recall time.
Map-reduce: extract per chunk then aggregate, forcing a full pass.
optionScenarioImpacts: 散落长尾的低相似事实照样排不进来，还塞爆上下文
远超任何窗口、中段信息被忽略，成本也爆炸
排得更准但仍只取几块，漏事实的结构没变
只有走遍全部 chunk 聚合，才能保证一处不漏
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Low-similarity scattered facts still stay out, and the context overflows.
It exceeds any window, ignores the middle, and cost explodes.
Ranking is sharper but you still take only a few chunks — the miss structure is unchanged.
Only a full pass over every chunk plus aggregation guarantees nothing is missed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 取回的结果里真正相关的比例——衡量「取的准不准」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision is the share of retrieved results that are actually relevant.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有相关内容里被取回的比例——衡量「漏没漏」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall is the share of all relevant content that was actually retrieved.

termDefinitions.meaning: map 阶段并行处理每个 chunk 产出局部结果，reduce 阶段把局部结果聚合成终答。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Map-reduce processes every chunk in parallel (map) then aggregates the partial results into a final answer (reduce).

optionDirectness: 只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
只有这个绝对假设成立时才适合。
只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
optionDirectness_en: Only fits when this statement is true: raise top-k from 5 to 1000 to pull in more chunks.
Only fits when this statement is true: concatenate all 100K pages into one huge context for a single read.
Only fits when this statement is true: swap in a stronger embedding model to improve relevance ranking.
Use when top-k optimizes precision and silently misses thinly scattered facts, so for completeness you must touch every chunk via map-reduce: map extracts per chunk, reduce aggregates.

scenario: 同一个法律 RAG 系统会收到两类问题——A:「合同第 7.2 条的赔偿上限是多少」；B:「把整个卷宗里所有和损害赔偿有关的内容都汇总出来」。
scenario_en: The same legal RAG system gets two kinds of questions — A: 'what is the cap in clause 7.2?' and B: 'summarize every damages-related item across the whole record'.
q: 哪一类问题必须遍历全量(map-reduce)，而不是 top-k 检索？
q_en: Which question requires a full pass (map-reduce) rather than top-k retrieval?
why: A 是「找唯一那条」——top-k 检索最直接。B 要求穷尽全卷、不能漏任何一处，只有遍历每个 chunk 的 map-reduce 能保证 recall。任务意图决定用哪条路径。
why_en: Finding one clause is retrieval, but summarizing every damages item across the record demands exhaustiveness, so only a map-reduce pass over all chunks guarantees recall.
tradeoff: 按意图选路径：找单点=检索 vs 穷尽全量=map-reduce
options: B(汇总全卷所有损害赔偿)——要穷尽不漏，必须遍历全量做 map-reduce
A(找第 7.2 条上限)——只此一条，也得遍历全量才稳妥
两者都用 top-k 检索即可，靠相似度排序取前几块就够
两者都得上 map-reduce，宁可全量遍历也不冒漏检风险
options_en: B (summarize all damages) — must be exhaustive, so a full map-reduce pass.
A (find the cap in clause 7.2) — just this one, but still needs a full pass to be safe.
Both just need top-k retrieval; ranking by similarity and taking the top few is enough.
Both should use map-reduce; better a full pass than risk missing something.
whenOtherWins: 对 A 这种「找唯一那条」的问题，top-k 检索又快又准；只有当任务要求「找出每一处」时才值得付 map-reduce 的成本。
optionExplanations: 对；B 要「全都要」，漏一处就错，必须遍历每个 chunk 聚合，这是 recall 任务。
A 只需命中一个明确事实，top-k 检索足够，遍历全量是浪费。
B 用 top-k 会漏掉散落在长尾的赔偿条目，无法保证穷尽。
A 用 map-reduce 是杀鸡用牛刀，徒增几千次 LLM 调用的延迟和成本。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — B needs everything; missing one item is wrong, so you must pass over every chunk and aggregate, a recall task.
A only needs one clear fact; top-k retrieval suffices and a full pass is wasteful.
Using top-k for B misses damages items scattered in the long tail and cannot guarantee exhaustiveness.
Using map-reduce for A is overkill, adding thousands of LLM calls in latency and cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 任务要求覆盖到每一处相关内容，一处不漏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exhaustiveness means the task must cover every relevant item without missing any.

scenario: 面试官追问：map-reduce 和 iterative refine 都能 touch 每个 chunk，你怎么选？
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: both map-reduce and iterative refine touch every chunk, so how do you choose?
q: map-reduce 和 iterative refine 的核心区别是什么？
q_en: What is the core difference between map-reduce and iterative refine?
why: map-reduce 并行处理每个 chunk 再一次性聚合，可横向扩展、快；refine 串行携带一个 running answer 逐块更新，保留跨块的连贯推理但没法并行。
why_en: Map-reduce processes chunks in parallel then aggregates, while refine carries a running answer serially through each chunk for coherent reasoning but no parallelism.
tradeoff: map-reduce(可并行、快) vs refine(串行、上下文连贯)
options: refine 并不需要读全部 chunk，靠采样其中几块串起来就能收敛
map-reduce 只做并行抽取局部结果，从不把它们产出成最终答案
map-reduce 并行 map 各块再一次 reduce；refine 串行更新 running answer
两者完全等价，只是并行时叫 map-reduce、串行时叫 refine
options_en: Refine need not read every chunk; sampling a few and stitching them converges.
Map-reduce only extracts partials in parallel and never yields them as a final answer.
Map-reduce maps chunks in parallel then reduces once; refine updates a running answer serially.
They are equivalent — one just calls parallel 'map-reduce' and serial 'refine'.
optionExplanations: 错；refine 同样要走遍每个 chunk，只是方式是串行更新而非并行。
错；reduce 阶段正是把局部结果聚合成最终答案。
对；map-reduce 靠并行拿吞吐，refine 靠串行携带上下文换连贯性。
错；一个可并行一个必须串行，扩展性和连贯性取舍完全不同。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect — refine also walks every chunk, just serially updating instead of in parallel.
Incorrect — the reduce step is exactly what aggregates partials into a final answer.
Correct — map-reduce buys throughput via parallelism, refine buys coherence via a serial running answer.
Incorrect — one parallelizes and one must be serial, a very different scalability/coherence tradeoff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 串行遍历每个 chunk，把一个滚动答案不断修订，保留跨块上下文。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Iterative refine walks chunks serially, revising a running answer while keeping cross-chunk context.

termDefinitions.meaning: refine 中携带并逐步更新的中间答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A running answer is the intermediate answer that refine carries and updates step by step.

scenario: 有人提议：既然新模型窗口有 200K token，干脆把 10 万页尽量塞进去让它一次读完。
scenario_en: Someone proposes: since the new model has a 200K-token window, just stuff in as many of the 100K pages as possible for a single read.
q: 直接堆超长上下文的主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of just dumping a huge context in?
why: 长上下文会 degrade——模型对中间内容注意力弱化(lost in the middle)、成本随 token 线性甚至更快上涨，而且 10 万页本就超窗口。应只让检索/压缩后的相关 context 进模型。
why_en: Long context degrades because the model attends poorly to the middle (lost in the middle) and cost balloons, so only retrieved or condensed context should reach the model.
options: 主要风险是 embedding 会因输入变长而在线重新计算，反过来拖慢整个离线索引管线
长上下文 degrade(lost in the middle)、成本爆炸且超窗口，只喂检索/压缩后的 context
主要风险是一旦超过窗口，模型就直接报错拒答，必须再加一层人工兜底流程
主要风险是向量库因这次查询变少而缓存失效，需要把索引整体重建一遍
options_en: The main risk is embeddings recomputing online as input grows, which in turn slows the whole offline indexing pipeline.
Long context degrades (lost in the middle), cost explodes, and it exceeds the window — feed only retrieved/condensed context.
The main risk is that once the window is exceeded the model hard-errors and refuses, requiring an extra manual fallback path.
The main risk is the vector store's cache going stale from fewer queries, requiring the whole index to be rebuilt.
optionMeanings: 把长上下文风险误当成离线 embedding 重算的问题
真正的风险：注意力稀释 + 成本 + 超窗口三合一
以为超窗口=模型硬性报错拒答
以为堆上下文会波及向量库的缓存与存储
optionMeanings_en: Mistakes the long-context risk for an offline embedding-recompute problem.
The real risk: attention dilution plus cost plus exceeding the window, all at once.
Assumes exceeding the window makes the model hard-error and refuse.
Assumes stuffing context spills over into vector-store cache and storage.
optionScenarioImpacts: embedding 离线早算好，与在线塞多少 context 无关
所以只把检索或压缩后的片段喂进模型，正解
模型不会拒答，只是中段信息被漏、质量下滑
上下文长短不影响向量库，两回事
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Embeddings were computed offline, unrelated to how much context you stuff online.
So feed only retrieved or condensed slices into the model — the right call.
The model does not refuse; it just drops middle facts and quality slips.
Context length does not touch the vector store — two different things.

termDefinitions.term: long-context degradation / lost in the middle
termDefinitions.meaning: 上下文越长，模型对中间部分的信息越容易忽略，答案质量下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Long-context degradation ('lost in the middle') is the model ignoring middle content as context grows, lowering answer quality.

optionDirectness: 只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
这是本题要识别的核心原因。
只有这个绝对假设成立时才适合。
适合临时加速或可容忍短暂旧值。
optionDirectness_en: Only fits when this statement is true: the main risk is embeddings recomputing online as input grows.
This is the core issue in this scenario.
Only fits when this statement is true: the main risk is that once the window is exceeded the model hard-errors and refuses.
Only fits when this statement is true: the main risk is the vector store's cache going stale from fewer queries.

scenario: 向量检索用 bi-encoder 快速召回 50 个候选 chunk，但前几名不总是最相关，而 prompt 只装得下 5 块。
scenario_en: Vector retrieval uses a bi-encoder to recall 50 candidate chunks fast, but the top few are not always the most relevant, and the prompt only fits 5.
q: 为什么要在 top-k 之后再加一层 rerank？
q_en: Why add a rerank stage after top-k retrieval?
why: bi-encoder 分开编码 query 和 chunk、快但粗；rerank 用 cross-encoder 把 query-chunk 成对读、精但慢。先召回 50 再精排出最相关的 5 块，把 prompt 预算花在刀刃上。
why_en: A bi-encoder recalls fast but coarsely, so a cross-encoder rerank reads each query-chunk pair jointly to pick the truly most relevant few for the limited prompt budget.
tradeoff: bi-encoder(快、粗召回) vs cross-encoder rerank(慢、精排)
options: rerank 能替代 embedding 和向量库，直接由它一步完成召回和排序
rerank 主要为了压缩索引，减少向量库的存储占用与成本
rerank 让整体检索更快，可以直接跳过精排、返回原始候选块
用 cross-encoder 成对精排 query-chunk，precision 更高，把最相关的几块塞进 prompt
options_en: Rerank replaces embeddings and the vector store, doing both recall and ranking in one step.
Rerank mainly compresses the index to cut vector-store storage and cost.
Rerank makes overall retrieval faster by skipping the fine ranking and returning raw candidates.
A cross-encoder reranks query-chunk pairs for higher precision, packing the most relevant few into the prompt.
whenOtherWins: 如果 bi-encoder 召回已经足够准、或延迟预算极紧，可以跳过 rerank 直接用 top-k。
optionMeanings: 以为 rerank 是召回层，能顶替向量检索
以为 rerank 的目的是省存储
以为 rerank 能给检索提速
cross-encoder 精排：把 query 和 chunk 拼一起联合打分
optionMeanings_en: Assumes rerank is a recall layer that can stand in for vector retrieval.
Assumes rerank exists to save storage.
Cross-encoder rerank: feed the query and chunk together for a joint score.
optionScenarioImpacts: 它只排序不召回，仍依赖 embedding 给的候选
它不碰存储，处理的是「召回后怎么排」
它逐对计算反而更慢，换来的是准不是快
把 50 个候选压成最相关的 5 块，正好塞满只装得下 5 块的窗口
optionScenarioImpacts_en: It only reorders, never recalls, and still relies on the embedding candidates.
It never touches storage; it decides ordering after recall.
Per-pair scoring is actually slower — it buys precision, not speed.
It narrows 50 candidates to the top 5, exactly filling the 5-slot budget.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分别把 query 和 chunk 编码成向量再比相似度，快但较粗。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bi-encoder embeds the query and chunk separately then compares vectors — fast but coarse.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 query 和 chunk 拼在一起送进模型联合打分，准但慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder feeds the query and chunk together for a joint relevance score — accurate but slow.

optionDirectness: 只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
只有题设改成这个方向时才适合。
这是本题要识别的核心原因。
optionDirectness_en: Only fits when this statement is true: rerank replaces embeddings and the vector store, doing both recall and ranking in one step.
Only fits when this statement is true: rerank mainly compresses the index to cut vector-store storage and cost.
Only fits when this statement is true: rerank makes overall retrieval faster by skipping the fine ranking and returning raw candidates.
This is the core issue in this scenario.

scenario: 法律检索既要语义匹配，又要精确命中案号、法条编号、当事人姓名这类 exact term，而向量检索对精确字符串并不敏感。
scenario_en: Legal search needs semantic matching plus exact hits on case numbers, statute IDs, and party names, but vector search is weak on exact strings.
q: 纯向量检索的短板该怎么补？
q_en: How do you cover the blind spot of pure vector search?
why: 向量擅长语义、但对精确 token(案号、法条编号)不敏感；加关键词/BM25 做 hybrid，向量管「意思相近」、关键词管「字面精确」，两路召回再合并。
why_en: Vector search handles semantics but misses exact tokens, so add keyword/BM25 for a hybrid where vectors catch meaning and keywords catch literal matches.
tradeoff: 向量(语义相近) vs 关键词(字面精确)，hybrid 两者兼得
options: 加关键词/BM25 做 hybrid：向量管语义、关键词管精确 term，两路召回合并
只用关键词检索，彻底放弃向量，丢掉同义改写的语义匹配
把 top-k 从 50 调到 5，用更小候选集提高命中精度
换一个更大的 LLM 来生成，靠模型能力补检索的缺口
options_en: Add keyword/BM25 for hybrid: vectors for semantics, keywords for exact terms, then merge.
Use only keyword search, drop vectors entirely, and lose paraphrase/synonym matches.
Lower top-k from 50 to 5, using a smaller candidate set to sharpen precision.
Swap in a larger LLM for generation, leaning on model power to cover retrieval gaps.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询都是自然语言语义问题、没有精确 ID/术语匹配需求，纯向量检索就够，不必加关键词一路。
optionExplanations: 对；hybrid 让语义和字面精确各司其职，案号、法条编号这类 exact term 不再漏。
只用关键词会丢掉同义/改写的语义匹配，法律问句常常不含原文原词。
调 top-k 改变的是取几块，改变不了向量对精确字符串不敏感的本质。
更大的 LLM 救不了「相关 chunk 根本没被检索到」，问题在检索层不在生成层。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — hybrid lets semantics and literal matching each do their job, so exact terms like case numbers stop being missed.
Keyword-only loses paraphrase/synonym matches, and legal questions rarely use the source's exact wording.
Tuning top-k changes how many chunks you take, not the fact that vectors are weak on exact strings.
A bigger LLM cannot fix chunks that were never retrieved; the problem is at retrieval, not generation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时用向量(语义)和关键词(字面)两路检索，再合并排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hybrid search combines vector (semantic) and keyword (literal) retrieval, then merges the rankings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 经典的关键词相关性打分算法，按词频/逆文档频率给文档打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BM25 is a classic keyword relevance scoring algorithm based on term frequency and inverse document frequency.

scenario: 生成的法律答案必须可溯源到具体文件页码，且绝不能编造引用——律师要能逐条核查。
scenario_en: Generated legal answers must trace back to specific file pages and must never fabricate citations — a lawyer needs to verify each claim.
q: 怎么保证答案 grounded(有据)且可核查？
q_en: How do you keep answers grounded and verifiable?
why: 每个 chunk 带 (文件, 页, chunk_id) 一路传到答案做 citation；生成后再把终答的每条 claim 对照检索到的 chunk 逐一 verify，抓出遗漏和幻觉。
why_en: Carry each chunk's (file, page, chunk_id) through to the answer as citations, then verify every claim against the retrieved chunks to catch omissions and hallucinations.
options: 让模型自由发挥，出了问题再靠人工事后逐句全量复查来兜底把关
chunk 带 (文件,页,chunk_id) 做 citation，每条 claim 对照 chunk verify
只返回检索到的 chunk 原文、完全不做生成，交给用户自己去读和判断
调高 temperature 让答案更丰富，靠华丽措辞掩盖引用上的不确定性
options_en: Let the model free-wheel, then have humans recheck every line by hand afterward as a fallback.
Carry (file, page, chunk_id) as citations, and verify each claim against its chunk.
Return only the retrieved chunk text and skip generation entirely, leaving users to read and judge.
Raise temperature so answers are richer, using fancy wording to paper over citation uncertainty.
optionExplanations: 全量人工复查不可扩展，也没利用元数据溯源，等于放任幻觉先发生。
对；元数据一路带到 citation 让答案可溯源，claim-vs-chunk 校验再兜住遗漏和编造。
只返回 chunk 就退化成搜索引擎，没完成「基于材料作答」这一步。
调高 temperature 只会加剧编造，与 grounding 目标相反。
optionExplanations_en: Full manual recheck does not scale, ignores metadata tracing, and lets hallucinations happen first.
Correct — metadata carried into citations makes answers traceable, and claim-vs-chunk checking catches omissions and fabrications.
Returning only chunks degrades to a search engine and skips answering from the material.
Raising temperature worsens fabrication, opposite to the grounding goal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 答案的每个论断都能对应到检索到的原文出处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Grounding means every claim in the answer maps back to a retrieved source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型编造出检索材料里并不存在的事实或引用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hallucination is a fact or citation the model fabricates that is not in the retrieved material.

q: 把「在 10 万页里找出每一处相关事实」的完整性决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the completeness decision chain for finding every relevant fact across 100K pages:
steps: 选型：map-reduce 遍历全部 chunk(map 逐块抽取 → reduce 聚合)
需求：法律任务要求穷尽，一处提及都不能漏(recall 优先)
代价：每个 chunk 一次 LLM 调用，成千上万次，延迟和成本高
缓解：并行 map、缓存部分结果、只 reduce 真正相关的
why: 合格的决策链 = 需求(穷尽/recall) → 选型(map-reduce 遍历全量) → 代价(数千次 LLM 调用) → 缓解(并行+缓存+精简 reduce)。面试就考你能把这条链讲完整。
why_en: A solid chain runs requirement (exhaustiveness) to choice (map-reduce over all chunks) to cost (thousands of LLM calls) to mitigation (parallelize, cache, reduce only what matters).
diagram:
flowchart LR R["需求：穷尽
一处不漏 (recall)"] --> C["选型：map-reduce
遍历全部 chunk"] C --> K["代价：数千次 LLM 调用
延迟/成本高"] K --> M["缓解：并行 map + 缓存
+ 只 reduce 相关的"]

termDefinitions.meaning: map 并行处理每个 chunk，reduce 聚合成终答，用来保证遍历全量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Map-reduce processes each chunk in parallel then aggregates, ensuring a full pass over the corpus.

scenario: map-reduce over 10 万页要跑几分钟、中途可能有 worker 崩溃，面试官问你怎么编排这个「扫批次→累积→合成」的多步生成。
scenario_en: Map-reduce over 100K pages runs for minutes and a worker may crash mid-run; the interviewer asks how you orchestrate this scan-accumulate-synthesize multi-step generation.
q: 怎么把这条多步 pipeline 建得可靠？
q_en: How do you build this multi-step pipeline reliably?
why: 建成显式 graph/状态机(节点=retrieve/map/reduce/verify)，typed state 携带累积进度；每步 checkpoint + 可重试 + 可观测，崩溃后从 checkpoint 续跑而非重来。
why_en: Model it as an explicit graph/state machine with typed state and per-node checkpointing, retries, and observability, so a crash resumes from a checkpoint instead of restarting.
tradeoff: 巨型单 prompt(简单但脆) vs 显式 graph state(可 checkpoint/恢复)
options: 写成一个巨大的 prompt 一次性调用完，让模型自己在内部管好所有步骤
用内存里的全局变量存 map 的中间结果，多个 worker 直接共享它
建显式 graph/状态机，typed state 携带进度，每步 checkpoint、可重试、可观测
任何一步失败就丢弃全部进度、整条 pipeline 从头重跑
options_en: Write one giant prompt and call it once, letting the model manage every step internally.
Keep map's intermediate results in global in-memory variables shared across workers.
Build an explicit graph/state machine with typed state carrying progress, per-step checkpoint, retry, and observability.
Discard all progress and restart the whole pipeline from scratch on any failure.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务只有一步、几秒内完成、失败重跑成本可忽略，一个直接的 LLM 调用就够，不必上状态机。
optionExplanations: 巨型 prompt 不可 checkpoint、崩了全丢，也塞不下 10 万页的中间态。
内存全局变量随进程崩溃一起消失，多 worker 也无法共享，谈不上恢复。
对；graph state 让每个节点独立 checkpoint/重试/观测，长跑崩溃可从断点续，正是 durable pipeline。
整条重跑浪费已完成的 map 结果，几分钟的任务反复失败会永远跑不完。
optionExplanations_en: A giant prompt cannot checkpoint, loses everything on crash, and cannot hold 100K pages of intermediate state.
Global in-memory variables vanish with the process and cannot be shared across workers, so no recovery.
Correct — graph state lets each node checkpoint/retry/observe independently, so a long run resumes from where it broke — a durable pipeline.
Restarting wastes completed map results, and a minutes-long task that keeps failing never finishes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多步 LLM 工作流建成图，节点是步骤、边携带带类型的累积状态(问题/chunk/局部答案/引用)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Graph state models a multi-step LLM workflow as a graph where nodes are steps and edges carry typed accumulated state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把中间进度持久化下来，崩溃后可从该点恢复而非重跑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint persists intermediate progress so a crash can resume from that point instead of restarting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 agent 工作流写成有状态图的编排框架，天然支持 checkpoint。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LangGraph is a framework for writing agent workflows as stateful graphs with built-in checkpointing.
